record.paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
record.original_question: In solar-wind turbulence at ion and electron kinetic scales, what is the physical nature of the fluctuations, and through which collisionless plasma mechanisms are those fluctuations dissipated? This question asks for a theory that can distinguish which competing collisionless processes are active at ion and electron scales and explain how they determine the observed kinetic-scale turbulent cascade and dissipation.

evidence.quote: A long-lasting debate concerns the nature of ion and electron scale fluctuations in solar-wind turbulence and their dissipation via collisionless plasma mechanisms.
several collisionless plasma processes may be simultaneously at play and compete with each other in determining the nature of ion-scale and electron-scale fluctuations

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a weakly collisional, magnetized plasma such as the solar wind, modeled by the Vlasov–Maxwell system for ion and electron distribution functions f_s(x,v,t) (s ∈ {i,e}) coupled to electromagnetic fields (E,B). Assume a turbulent state in which energy injected at large (magnetohydrodynamic) scales cascades to smaller scales, crossing the ion kinetic scales (ion gyroradius ρ_i and ion inertial length d_i) and continuing down to the electron kinetic scales (ρ_e, d_e), where it is ultimately converted into particle internal energy (heating) by collisionless mechanisms.

Candidate collisionless dissipation/cascade mechanisms that may operate simultaneously include: (i) linear and nonlinear Landau damping on ions and electrons; (ii) cyclotron (ion or electron) resonant damping; (iii) stochastic ion heating by low-frequency, large-amplitude fluctuations; (iv) magnetic reconnection in current sheets formed by the cascade; (v) dissipation in coherent structures such as current sheets and vortices; (vi) wave–particle interactions associated with kinetic Alfvén waves, whistler waves, and ion-Bernstein modes.

Problem. Develop a predictive theory of the kinetic-scale turbulent cascade in such a plasma that:
(a) Determines, from the plasma parameters (e.g. ion and electron plasma betas β_i, β_e, ion-to-electron temperature ratio T_i/T_e, and the angle θ between the local mean magnetic field and the cascade wavevector), the physical nature of the fluctuations at sub-ion scales (k ρ_i ≳ 1) and at sub-electron scales (k ρ_e ≳ 1) — in particular, the relative weight of kinetic Alfvén-wave-like, whistler-like, and non-wavelike (e.g. coherent structure) fluctuations and their anisotropy in k-space.
(b) Identifies which of the candidate collisionless mechanisms above dominates the conversion of fluctuation energy into ion and electron heating in each regime, and quantifies the resulting partition of energy between parallel and perpendicular ion heating, electron heating, and any non-thermal particle acceleration.
(c) Predicts, as a function of these parameters, the spectral indices, spectral break scales, and amplitude ratios of magnetic, electric, and density fluctuations in the kinetic range, in a manner falsifiable by comparison with fully kinetic 3D-in-space, 3D-in-velocity Vlasov–Maxwell simulations and in situ spacecraft measurements.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open question in space plasma physics. As of 2024–2026, no single theory uniquely identifies the nature of sub-ion and sub-electron scale fluctuations and their dominant collisionless dissipation channel; competing mechanisms (Landau damping, cyclotron damping, stochastic heating, reconnection, dissipation in coherent structures) are all observed to contribute under different conditions in Parker Solar Probe / MMS data and in 3D3V kinetic simulations. Recent reviews continue to describe it as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic turbulence in astrophysical plasmas: waves and/or structures? (Schekochihin et al., review)
status_evidence.snippet: The nature of kinetic-range fluctuations and the dominant dissipation mechanism in collisionless plasma turbulence remain debated; both wavelike and structure-based pictures persist.
status_evidence.claim: As of recent reviews, the nature of ion/electron-scale fluctuations and their collisionless dissipation is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: MMS observations of energy conversion at kinetic scales (review, 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Multiple processes — Landau damping, stochastic heating, reconnection, and dissipation in coherent structures — are simultaneously observed to channel turbulent energy into particles.
status_evidence.claim: Several collisionless processes are observed to contribute, with no consensus on a unique dominant mechanism.
